_about: Where Amass reads routing security records for a netblock, and which routing-registry maintainers say nothing about who runs it. RIPEstat (stat_api) answers for every region with no key: its whois data call returns the Internet Routing Registry (IRR) route objects for a prefix, each with its origin AS and maintainer (mnt-by), and its rpki-validation call returns the RPKI validity of a prefix and origin AS with the ROAs that cover it. irr_whois is a routing registry whois server that answers inverse queries (-i mnt-by <maintainer>), listing every route object one maintainer keeps across the registries it mirrors; RADb mirrors the major ones. A maintainer is an operator's account in the registry, and operators reuse one across all their route objects, so it is the routing counterpart of a shared registrant. registry_maintainers are prefixes of maintainer handles the registries themselves use for allocations, legacy space and RPKI-generated objects: they name the registry, not the operator, and are never used. max_routes is the most route objects a maintainer may keep for its other route objects to count: a maintainer keeping more is an ISP, hosting provider or registry keeping objects for many customers. max_origins likewise bounds the origin ASes across one maintainer's route objects.
